quota-reservation-under-concurrency-01.graded_text: Starting an upload atomically reserves its declared size against remaining capacity, counting other open reservations, so parallel uploads cannot together pass the cap. A check of used plus size alone is identified as insufficient.

votes.e: B/project/docs/quota-accounting.md:23 "**Admission rule:** a new upload of `size` bytes is admitted only if `used + reserved + size <= cap`, evaluated inside a serializable transaction that also inserts the reservation. Concurrent starts therefore serialize, and the eighth file in a batch sees the first seven's reservations." The old check is named as insufficient at line 7/9: "The old flow checked `used + size <= cap` ... The check ignored uploads already started but not yet finalized." Code: B/project/packages/backend/src/uploads.ts:46-47 `const reserved = await openReservedBytes(tx, ctx.accountId, now); if (account.used + reserved + input.size > account.cap) {` inside `ctx.db.transaction`, followed by the insert at line 50.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-02.graded_text: Finalize commits usage from the verified stored size and turns the reservation into usage, and a failed, abandoned, or expired upload releases its reservation through a stated cleanup path.

votes.e: B/project/packages/backend/src/uploads.ts:105-106 `await tx.accounts.patch(account.id, { used: account.used + stored.size }); await tx.uploads.patch(current.id, { status: "ready", size: stored.size, finalizedAt: now });`, which charges the measured size (line 76 "Charge what storage actually holds, never what the client declared.") and turns the pending reservation into usage. Release paths: B/project/docs/quota-accounting.md:21 "an expired reservation stops counting at expiry without waiting for a job", line 54 `cancelUpload` "Releases the reservation immediately", and line 58 `sweepUnfinalizedUploads` marks still-pending rows `expired` and deletes the bytes, all coded at uploads.ts:118-147. Size mismatch -> `rejected` (line 88) also releases.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-03.graded_text: A retried finalize counts the upload's size once, not twice, in both the design and the changed code.

votes.e: Design: B/project/docs/quota-accounting.md:47 "If the upload is already `ready`, it returns success and changes nothing. Retries are safe." and line 49 "each upload gets exactly one summary job however many times finalize runs." Code: B/project/packages/backend/src/uploads.ts:73 `if (upload.status === "ready") return { uploadId: upload.id, size: upload.size };` and inside the transaction line 84 `if (current.status === "ready") return { kind: "ready", size: current.size };` before the increment at line 105.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-04.graded_text: The user's storage quota is kept separate from the model provider's cost: the design says a failed summary can still cost the product money and records or bounds that cost, rather than promising failed work is free.

votes.e: B keeps storage and provider cost apart in name: B/project/docs/quota-accounting.md:67 "**Provider cost is a separate ledger from the storage cap.** The product pays per summary whether or not the user's storage allowance is touched." But it never says a failed summary attempt still costs money, and it never records or bounds that cost. No cost ledger is defined in the doc or the code (B/project/packages/backend/src/uploads.ts has no summary accounting at all). The only per-account bound is deferred: doc line 88 "I recommend a hidden daily (or monthly) cap on summaries per account ... The number is a cost decision, so I didn't invent one." The closest line is doc line 66 "A summary is never auto-retried. It is paid provider work". That limits automatic retries per upload, but it neither records spend nor caps it. Line 65 "A failed or cancelled upload never costs a model call" covers uploads, not failed summaries.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-05.graded_text: Finalize compares the actual stored size with the reserved size and refuses or corrects a mismatch, so a client cannot reserve a small size and store a large object.

votes.e: B/project/packages/backend/src/uploads.ts:87-89 `if (stored.size !== current.size) { await tx.uploads.patch(current.id, { status: "rejected" }); return { kind: "size_mismatch" }; }` -> line 112 `throw new InvalidUpload("size_mismatch")`, with the PUT bound to the declared size at line 61 `signPut(upload.id, { size: upload.size, expiresAt: upload.expiresAt })`. Design: B/project/docs/quota-accounting.md:49 "rechecks the status, rejects a size mismatch, adds the **measured** size to `used`" and line 40 "Signs a PUT bound to the exact `Content-Length`".

blocking: [claude-fallback] B ships the free-plan opening with no bound on provider spend. It identifies upload-and-delete loops as a way to burn the model budget without touching the cap, then leaves the limit undecided instead of committing to one, even a placeholder: B/project/docs/quota-accounting.md:88 "I recommend a hidden daily (or monthly) cap on summaries per account ... The number is a cost decision, so I didn't invent one." Nothing in B/project/packages/backend/src/uploads.ts limits `tx.jobs.enqueue("summarize", ...)` (line 108) per account.
